title: Lives and Game Over (bonus)
body:
Goal: add a second variable, lives, and end the game when it reaches 0. Tool: Scratch app (offline). Start from: your apple-catch project.

Build steps

  1. Open apple-catch (File > Load from your computer).
  2. Make a variable lives (For all sprites).
  3. Click the Apple. Under set score to 0, add set lives to 3.
  4. Inside the if (y position) < -170 block (a missed apple), add change lives by -1 above the go to block.
  5. At the bottom of the forever loop, add the game-over check below.
  6. Test: miss three apples on purpose. Then click the flag and play properly.
  7. Save as apple-catch-lives.

The script in words (new parts)

Apple sprite, inside the green-flag script:

  • set lives to 3 (under set score to 0)
  • inside "if (y position) < -170": change lives by -1
  • at the bottom of the forever loop:
    • if lives = 0 then
      • say "Game over!" for 2 seconds
      • stop all

Expected behavior

Each game starts with 0 points and 3 lives. Every missed apple takes away one life. Catches still add 1 point. When lives reach 0, the apple says "Game over!" and the whole game stops.

Checklist

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Open your apple-catch project and click the Apple. You are adding a second counter, so look in the Variables category and at the missed-apple if block.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Make a variable named lives. Set it at the start of the game, just like score. Lose a life only in the if block for a missed apple, not in the catch block. Then add a new if at the bottom of the forever loop to check for zero lives.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: The game-over check is an if block (Control category) with an = block (Operators category) and the lives variable in it. Inside it, put a say block (Looks category), then stop all (Control category). Use set lives to ____ and change lives by ____.
